BusyChannel.description:
Busy channel with a relationship to a ResourceBase.
Id corresponds to a busy channel number (0-15 for RODBusyModule; 0-2 for LTP, 0-4 for CTPOUT, etc): the channel number where the busy cable is plugged into.
The ResourceBase should be the corresponding Resource where the busy is formed. Depending on the Resource, the BusyChannel can be taken into account or ignored.
Examples:
- ROD for a RODBusy channel
- RODBusyModule for a RODBusyModule (the busy that goes out of the RODBusy comes from itself, from the internal OR of its busy channels)
- RCDLTPModule for RCDLTPModule (similar to RODBusyModule)
- if no resource is available in the database, an ad-hoc Resource can be created. By putting it into the Resources relationship of a segment, one can enable/disable it conveniently.

Output class for the IO Manager to
send events to a circular buffer.
Can work in both master and 
slave mode, either pretending 
to write out all the events
or to skip them when the output
buffer is full.

OutputCircName.description: This is the name of the output circular buffer.

SamplingGap.description:
Define the minimum gap between two sampled
events. As a consequence, a maximum sampling 
ratio is defined.
If the ThrowIfFull parameter is true,
sampled event can be skipped if the buffer is
full, else all the events are written as soon
as there is room in the buffer.
The default value (1) means that all the events
are sent to the output, 0 means that no event
is sent.

BufferSize.description:
The size of the circular buffer to be used.
BufferSize=0 means that the access will be 
in slave mode (i.e., the buffer is created 
by someone else).

ThrowIfFull.description:
If the ThrowIfFull parameter is true,
sampled event can be skipped if the buffer is
full, else all the events are written as soon
as there is room in the buffer, thus generating
backpressure.

RunsOn.description:
Describe where to run template application.
For a segment the list of hosts is defined by "Hosts" relationship.
For template segment the list of hosts is defined by rack's hosts.
The "FirstHost" is first host in the list in state "On" without a possibility to restart application on a backup host.
The "FirstHostWithBackup" is similar to above and allows to restart application on one of enabled hosts.

2) "AllButFirstHost" is set, but there is only one segment host in state "On"

DataAccess.description:
An object of this class defines the number of ROBs selected
and from what subdetector[Group] they are selected.

Note that all ROBs from a subdetector or subdetectorGroup can be 
selected by one DataAccess object.

Note that if nROBDistribution and Subdetector
both evaluates to zero, no ROBs are selected.

subDetector.description:
If this value is 
0) ROBs from all available SubDetectors 
   (eformat::FULL_SD_EVENT) are selected.
1) in the range [1..0xf] ROBs from this 
   subDetectorGroup are selected.
2) in the range [0x10..0xff] ROBs from this 
   subDetector are selected.

nROBDistribution.description:
This attribute determines the number of ROB's to be requested. 
What ROBs can be selected depends on the setting of the subDetector attribute.

The value for nROBDistribution can be configured to be constant, 
a Root function or a Root histogram, see class dccommon::Distribution.

Complexity.description:
Define level of complexity of test.
When testing of a component is requested with the level 
specified, only those tests with a complexity <= the specified 
level are executed.
If no specific level is requested, all tests are executed.

Validity.description:
Amount of seconds during which a test result is valid.
This attribute is used by hte TM client library to avoid useless repetition of tests.

RepeatIfUnresolved.description:

automatically repeated before passing the result to the requestor.

ExecDependsOnSuccess.description:
The test will only be executed once the tests listed
in this relationship will have run successfully.

ExecDependsOnFailure.description:
The test will only be executed once the tests listed
in this relationship will have failed.

Failures.description:
Describes how the test can fail.
If this relation is left empty, a test failure will
not provide any hint on how to understand/debug/fix the problem.

RM_Resource.description:
The Resource class is used to describe shared and exclusive resources used by the processes: the name of the resource, the maximum numbers of copies per partition and per system (i.e. total), and documentation (help URL and comments). The dynamic part of a resource includes the list of processes that allocated this resource.
An example of a resource could be a run-time license (for example we can start limited number of processes with GUI that use some commercial widget). A resource can describe some hardware resources (for example we can not have two concurrent processes that write on the same type recorder device). The use of resources can be connected with the architecture of the process (for example, we do not want to allow start simultaneously several GUI editors for the same data, if there is no concurrent update of graphical view or the creator of software objects knows that it must be started only once per system or per partition, etc.).

For a segment the list of hosts is defined by "Hosts" relationship.
For template segment the list of hosts is defined by rack's hosts.
The "FirstHost" is first host in the list in state "On" without a possibility to restart application on a backup host.

For template segment the list of hosts is defined by rack's hosts.
The "FirstHost" is first host in the list in state "On" without a possibility to restart application on a backup host.

RunsOn.description:
Describe where to run template application.
For a segment the list of hosts is defined by "Hosts" relationship.
For template segment the list of hosts is defined by rack's hosts.
The "FirstHost" is first host in the list in state "On" without a possibility to restart application on a backup host.
The "FirstHostWithBackup" is similar to above and allows to restart application on one of enabled hosts.
Error is raised if:
1) "FirstHost" or "AllHosts" is set, but there are no segment hosts in state "On"
2) "AllButFirstHost" is set, but there is only one segment host in state "On"
